Everything else is explanation.\n28\t\n29\t---\n30\t\n31\t## 1. Objective\n32\t\n33\t> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n34\t> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n35\t> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n36\t>\n37\t> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n38\t\n39\t- **Static.** No backend. Files on a CDN, works offline, auditable once and trusted\n40\t  thereafter. There is nowhere to upload anything *to*.\n41\t- **Same page, both roles.** One deployment; the user picks sender or receiver.\n42\t- **Screen → camera is the only channel.** Strictly one-way, lossy, low-bandwidth.\n43\t- **Multi-gigabyte.** The requirement that most shapes the architecture (§3).\n44\t\n45\t### 1.1 The honest framing of \"multiple gigabytes\"\n46\t\n47\tMulti-GB support is an **architectural** requirement, not a performance promise. The\n48\tdesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\n49\tBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n50\t\n51\t| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n52\t|---|---|---|---|\n53\t| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n54\t| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n55\t| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n56\t| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n57\t| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n58\t\n59\t> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n60\t> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n61\t> one would overstate throughput.\n62\t\n63\t**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\n64\tand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n65\t\n66\t1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n67\t2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n68\t3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n69\t   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n70\t\n71\t---\n72\t\n73\t## 2. Glossary\n74\t\n75\tSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n76\t(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Within this\n77\tplan they mean exactly this:\n78\t\n79\t| Term | Meaning here |\n80\t|---|---|\n81\t| **Fragment** | The atomic unit the fountain code operates over. Fixed length **L** for the whole session (D15). |\n82\t| **K** | Number of fragments in one block. Derived as `blockSize / L`; never transmitted (D7). |\n83\t| **Block** | A contiguous slice of the (possibly compressed) payload, cut into K fragments and fountain-coded independently. **Always means this** — never \"fountain block\" or \"QR block\". |\n84\t| **Packet** | One fountain-coded symbol: 13-byte header + L payload bytes. The unit a tile carries. |\n85\t| **Tile** | One QR symbol on screen. Carries exactly one packet. |\n86\t| **Frame** | One displayed image, containing a grid of tiles. **Never** a video frame — those are *camera frames*. |\n87\t| **Camera frame** | One image captured by the receiver's camera. |\n88\t| **Beacon** | A special frame carrying file-level metadata instead of payload (D17, §7.2). |\n89\t| **Profile** | A modulation configuration: QR version, module pixel size, tile count. Several coexist per frame (D16). |\n90\t| **Dwell** | How many packets the sender emits for one block before advancing (§8.1). |\n91\t| **Screen px** | A pixel on the *sender's display*. What the renderer controls. |\n92\t| **Camera px** | A pixel in the *receiver's captured frame*. What the decoder actually sees. |\n93\t| **px/module** | **Always CAMERA px per module unless explicitly written \"screen px/module\".** The 4 px/module decode cliff is a *camera*-pixel figure. Conflating the two put every S2/S3 optical run below the cliff — see `../notes/spike-results.md` §S3. |\n94\t| **Magnification** | `camera_px_per_module = screen_px_per_module × M`, where `M` = (capture width across the code region) / (code region width in screen px). A 1920-px-wide landscape code region filling a 1080-px-wide portrait capture gives **M = 0.5625**, so 4 screen px/module is only **2.25 camera px/module**. |\n95\t| **Erasure** | A packet that did not arrive or failed validation. Never a corrupted packet — those are discarded, not used. |\n96\t| **Stage** | A modulation generation: 1 = tiled mono QR, 2 = + RGB tripling, 3 = custom grid codec. |\n97\t| **Pass** | One complete traversal of every block by the sender. |\n98\t\n99\t---\n100\t\n101\t## 3. What multi-gigabyte breaks, and the fix\n102\t\n103\tFour assumptions in the pre-multi-GB design do not survive contact with a 4 GB file.\n104\t\n105\t### 3.1 The fountain decoder does not scale — in TIME, not memory\n106\t\n107\tThis is the correction the plan review surfaced, and it matters because the first\n108\tversion of this section got it half right.\n109\t\n110\tD5 chose an LT code with a **Gaussian elimination** decoder, verified at\n111\t[`sim/`](../research/sim/). GE costs O(K²) in *memory* and O(K³) in *bit operations*.\n112\tThe original block-layer decision sized K from the memory term alone and concluded 4 MB\n113\tblocks (K = 16,384) were fine because the coefficient matrix is only 32 MB.\n114\t\n115\t**The memory term was never the binding constraint. Time is.**\n116\t\n117\tEach arriving packet is reduced against up to `rank` stored pivot rows; each row\n118\toperation XORs the coefficient mask (K/8 bytes) *and* the payload (L bytes). Reaching\n119\tfull rank costs `W = 2 · (K²/2) · (K/8 + L) = K² · (K/8 + L)` bytes of memory traffic,\n120\tand the block only lasts `K·L / R` seconds at wire rate R — so the decoder must\n121\t**sustain**:\n122\t\n123\t```\n124\trequired = W / (K·L/R) = K · (K/8 + L) · R / L    bytes/sec\n125\t```\n126\t\n127\t> The leading factor is **1, not 2** — the 2 and the /2 in `W` cancel. A previous\n128\t> revision of this section printed `2 · K · (K/8 + L) · R / L` and was 2× too\n129\t> pessimistic in every derived figure. Gate **G7** now diffs this section against the\n130\t> model so the class of error cannot recur.\n131\t\n132\tAll figures below are emitted by\n133\t[`sim/ge_cost_model.py`](../research/sim/ge_cost_model.py) — this section quotes the\n134\tmodel rather than reasoning beside it. **All rows at Stage 1 (R = 30 KB/s)**, so they\n135\tare comparable:\n136\t\n137\t| K | L | Block | Matrix | Work/block | Sustained need | |\n138\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n139\t| 1,000 | 1260 | 1.2 MB | 122.1 KB | 1.3 GB | 33.8 MB/s | research baseline |\n140\t| 1,500 | 1260 | 1.8 MB | 274.7 KB | 3.0 GB | 52.9 MB/s | research partitioning ceiling |\n141\t| 4,000 | 1260 | 4.8 MB | 1.9 MB | 26.2 GB | 171.6 MB/s | research called this **\"too slow\"** |\n142\t| **16,384** | **256** | **4.0 MB** | **32.0 MB** | **576.0 GB** | **4.5 GB/s** | **23× over budget** |\n143\t\n144\tThe plan's own evidence base\n145\t([`fountain-codes-and-protocol.md`](../research/fountain-codes-and-protocol.md) §2.6)\n146\tstates: *\"Cost scales as K², so it must be bounded. At K = 4000 the decode work is ~16×\n147\tthat of K = 1000 (~6 GB of XOR) — too slow\"* and recommends *\"source-block partitioning\n148\tabove K ≈ 1500\"*. **K = 16,384 was 11× past that ceiling.**\n149\t\n150\tIt was worse than a simple overshoot: shrinking L to 256 B to fit small tiles made the\n151\tmask term (K/8 = 2048 B) dominate the payload term (256 B) by 8×, so the decode problem\n152\tgot *harder* as a side effect of a decision made for a different reason.\n153\t\n154\t**Two further findings from the model:**\n155\t\n156\t- **A faster wire rate makes decode harder** — same work, less time to do it. So K MUST\n157\t  be sized for the *fastest* stage we intend to reach (Stage 3, 106 KB/s), not the\n158\t  slowest. This is counterintuitive and is why the original error was easy to make.\n159\t- **The sender's cost was unbudgeted too.** §6.3.1 counted QR encode and render but not\n160\t  the fountain XOR. At uncapped harmonic degree and K = 16,384 that is 398 KB of XOR\n161\t  per packet — **91.8 MB/s** at the old 225 packets/s (1 packet/tile), or **183.6 MB/s**\n162\t  at the adopted 450 packets/s (2 packets/tile at R2 nominal), on top of everything\n163\t  else. Hence D25.\n164\t\n165\t**Fix — D19:** K = **768**, L = **256 B**, block = **192.0 KB**.\n166\t\n167\t| | Was | Now |\n168\t|---|---|---|\n169\t| K | 16,384 | **768** |\n170\t| L | 256 B | **256 B** (unchanged — see §3.1.1) |\n171\t| Block | 4 MB | **192.0 KB** |\n172\t| GE matrix | 32.0 MB | **72.0 KB** |\n173\t| Block-layer working set | ~36 MB (claimed) | **264.0 KB** |\n174\t| Sustained need @ Stage 3 | 14.9 GB/s | **114.6 MB/s** |\n175\t\n176\t*Both \"sustained need\" figures are at Stage 3, so they compare like with like. The\n177\t4.5 GB/s in the table above is the same design at Stage 1.*\n178\t\n179\t**K_max at Stage 3 is 1152.** We adopt **768** deliberately below the ceiling —\n180\tD26 requires the sender to assume the weaker receiver, and the 200 MB/s budget is\n181\titself an unmeasured estimate (§18 R1). Margin at Stage 3: **1.74×**.\n182\t\n183\t| K | Block | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3 | |\n184\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n185\t| 512 | 128.0 KB | 19.7 MB/s | 39.3 MB/s | 69.5 MB/s | 2.88× margin |\n186\t| **768** | **192.0 KB** | **32.4 MB/s** | **64.9 MB/s** | **114.6 MB/s** | **adopted, 1.74× margin** |\n187\t| 1024 | 256.0 KB | 47.2 MB/s | 94.4 MB/s | 166.7 MB/s | 1.20× margin |\n188\t| 1152 | 288.0 KB | 55.3 MB/s | 110.6 MB/s | 195.4 MB/s | 1.02× — the ceiling |\n189\t| 1536 | 384.0 KB | 82.6 MB/s | 165.2 MB/s | 291.8 MB/s | 1.5× **over** at Stage 3 |\n190\t\n191\t### 3.1.1 L is set by the *conservative* ladder rung, not the nominal one\n192\t\n193\tA revision of this plan briefly set L = 507 B (\"one packet per v15 tile\") and broke\n194\tD16's ladder. D15's source note states the governing rule plainly: **pick L to fit the\n195\tsmallest tile any profile would use.** At L = 507 the packet is 520 B and the\n196\tconservative rung, v10-L, holds **271 B** — so it could carry **zero** packets, only\n197\tbeacons. That destroys the ladder's one load-bearing property: *a mis-guessed profile\n198\tyields zero; a ladder always yields something.*\n199\t\n200\t**Rungs are therefore defined by packet count, with the QR version chosen to fit** —\n201\tnot the reverse. At L = 256 B, packet = 13 + 256 = **269 B**:\n202\t\n203\t| Rung | Packets | Needs | QR version | Capacity | Waste |\n204\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n205\t| R1 conservative | 1 | 269 B | v10-L | 271 B | 2 B |\n206\t| R2 nominal | 2 | 538 B | v16-L | 586 B | 48 B |\n207\t| R3 aggressive | 3 | 807 B | v20-L | 858 B | 51 B |\n208\t| R4 (probe only) | 4 | 1076 B | v23-L | 1091 B | 15 B |\n209\t\n210\tWaste stays ≤ 51 B on every rung. The pressure that motivated raising L has also\n211\tgone: at K = 768 the mask term is K/8 = 96 B against a 256 B payload (27%), not the\n212\t8× dominance that made L = 256 pathological at K = 16,384.\n213\t\n214\t**A rung MUST carry a whole number of packets.** Partial packets across tiles would\n215\tcouple tiles together and destroy the independence D1 depends on.\n216\t\n217\t### 3.2 Neither side can hold the file in memory\n218\t\n219\tA multi-GB `Uint8Array` is not allocatable (Chrome's `ArrayBuffer` ceiling is ~2 GB;\n220\tSafari's is lower), and would get a phone tab killed regardless.\n221\t\n222\t**Fix — D20:** stream both ends. `File.slice()` on the sender, OPFS on the receiver, one\n223\tblock resident at a time.\n224\t\n225\t### 3.3 The whole-file hash cannot be computed in one pass\n226\t\n227\t`crypto.subtle.digest` has **no streaming API** — it takes one buffer.\n228\t\n229\t**Fix:** per-block hashes (cheap, and they let each block be verified and written the\n230\tmoment it completes) plus an optional whole-file hash from an incremental WASM hasher.\n231\tSee §7.4 for how this interacts with `streamId`.\n232\t\n233\t### 3.4 Miss recovery gets expensive as blocks multiply\n234\t\n235\tAt 192 KB per block a 4 GB file is ~21,800 blocks. Sequential dwell means a block missed\n236\ton pass 1 waits for pass 2 — hours. **Fix:** the repair code (§8.2), which makes recovery\n237\tsub-minute and is why smaller blocks are affordable.\n238\t\n239\t---\n240\t\n241\t## 4. Decisions\n242\t\n243\t| # | Decision | Rationale | Source |\n244\t|---|---|---|---|\n245\t| **D19** | **Block layer: independent 192.0 KB blocks, K = 768, L = 256 B** | GE cost is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). K = 768 keeps pace at Stage 3's 106 KB/s (114.6 MB/s needed, **1.74x margin**) within a conservative 200 MB/s phone-JS budget; matrix is 72.0 KB and the block-layer working set 264.0 KB, flat regardless of file size. K_max is 1152; 768 is deliberate conservatism per D26. **L is set by the conservative ladder rung** (S3.1.1), not the nominal one. What RFC 6330 calls source blocks. | §3.1, `sim/ge_cost_model.py` |\n246\t| **D27** | **The receiver duty-cycles under thermal pressure; multi-GB is framed as multi-session** | Measured: a Pixel 6 hit 70 °C and its throttling threshold in **20–30 minutes**, against a §1.1 objective of 27 h–4 days of *continuous* decoding. Duty-cycling is **nearly free on this channel** — a skipped frame is an erasure the fountain code already absorbs (D5) — so 50% duty roughly halves heat for roughly half the rate, and **finishes** where 100% duty may not. Drop decode *resolution* before dropping frames (superlinearly cheaper). No web API exposes SoC temperature, so sustained fps decline is the proxy (E17b). | `spike-results`, R11 |\n247\t| **D25** | **Cap fountain degree at d ≤ 64** | Cuts encoder XOR **7.9×** at the adopted K = 768 (mean degree 106.3 → 13.5): 12.2 MB/s → 1.6 MB/s at 450 packets/s (R2 nominal: 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps). D6 forbids changing the distribution on faith, so it was **simulated**: at the adopted **K = 768** the cap costs **+1.6 points** (1.34% → 2.97% mean, p99 4.2%), and +1.9 pts at K = 1024. There is a cliff below it — cap 32 costs +4.9 pts with a bad p99, cap 16 costs **+55 pts**. 64 is the right side of the cliff with margin. | `sim/degree_cap_sim.py` |\n248\t| **D26** | **K is chosen by the SENDER at session start and MUST be conservative** | Decode cost lands on the receiver, whose CPU the sender cannot know (no back-channel). So the sender MUST assume the weaker device. K = 768 is the default floor; a sender-side setting MAY raise it when the user knows the receiver is a desktop. The receiver derives K from the beacon and MUST refuse a stream whose K exceeds what it benchmarked locally. | §3.1 |\n249\t| **D20** | **Stream both ends; never materialise the file** | Multi-GB `ArrayBuffer` is not allocatable. `File.slice()` sender-side, OPFS receiver-side. | §3.2 |\n250\t| **D21** | **Per-packet header stays 13 bytes: file metadata lives in the beacon** | A 3-byte block index would have cost 23% more header. Moving `payloadLen`, filename, MIME, hash and block count into the periodic beacon pays for it exactly. Payload packets carry only what is needed to *place bytes*. | §7.1 |\n251\t| **D22** | **Resume is mandatory and first-class** | At 2.7–27 h for 1–10 GB, no transfer survives on user patience. Receiver persists the completed-block bitmap; incomplete blocks restart rather than persisting partial GE state. | §1.1, §8.3 |\n252\t| **D23** | **Estimate time before the user commits; refuse or warn at defined thresholds** | Thresholds are numeric (§13.1), not \"a threshold\". Estimate from *measured* rate once acquired. | §1.1 |\n253\t| **D24** | **Frames generated on demand and discarded; nothing pre-rendered** | The LT stream is endless — no finite frame set exists. One pass over 4 GB is ~550,000 frames = **4.2 TB** as `ImageData`. On-demand encode costs ~7% of one core. PRNG-derived indices make the sender **stateless**: frame *N* generates without replaying 1…*N*−1, which is what makes resume and repair nearly free. | §6.3.1 |\n254\t| D1 | **Tiled QR, not single QR** | 15 × v15 QR decode from one 1080p frame in 7.8 ms for ~7.5 KB user-visible payload (at 2 packets/tile: 15 tiles × 2 packets × 256 B = 7,680 B; 8.0 KB includes 13-byte headers). This vs 2,953 B for one v40 — ~2.5× for zero new decoder risk. | `beyond-qr` §10 |\n255\t| D2 | **QR v15 @ ECC L, ~15 tiles** | Bounded by the 4 **camera** px/module cliff (§2 — *not* screen px), not symbology density. EC L because the channel is erasure-dominated — redundancy belongs in the fountain code. L→H would cost 57% of payload for nothing. | `qr-encoding` |\n256\t| D3 | **zxing-wasm decoder, read `.bytes`** | Only credible multi-symbol decoder that returns real bytes — verified against 7 libraries with every byte value: exact in 100% of payloads. Bounded 9–26 ms where jsQR hit 1453 ms. Apache-2.0. | `browser-qr-scanning` |\n257\t| D4 | **node-qrcode encoder, mask pinned** | Pinning the mask is a 4.6–8× encode speedup — a bigger lever than library choice. Worker-safe. | `qr-encoding` |\n258\t| D5 | **LT fountain + harmonic distribution + GF(2) Gaussian elimination** | GE needs +1.2% overhead at K=1000 where peeling needs +180%. ~300 lines. **Re-measured at the adopted K = 768**: +1.34% mean / +2.5% p99 uncapped, +2.97% / +4.2% with D25's cap — inside §13.1's budget. See §18 R1 for the RaptorQ trigger. | `fountain-codes`, `sim/` |\n259\t| D6 | **Harmonic and GE are a coupled pair — never change one alone** | Harmonic + peeling is the worst cell measured and degrades as K grows. Fails only on large inputs, pointing away from the cause. Any change to the distribution (including D25's cap) MUST be simulated first. | `sim/` |\n260\t| D7 | **Index sets derived from a PRNG, never transmitted** | Seeded on `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`. Zero index bytes on the wire. | `fountain-codes` |\n261\t| D8 | **Compress before blocking, to a staging file** | `CompressionStream` is native and streaming. Compress to OPFS first, then cut into fixed blocks — keeps K constant and derivable. Skip on already-compressed input (sample-detect). Staging MUST be wiped (§12, T4a). **Trade-off: with compression enabled, resume is NOT supported** (§8.3, `notes/bf-17s0-resume-compression-conflict.md`) — `CompressionStream` offers no determinism guarantee, so re-compression after staging is reaped (E11) would produce different blocks and silently corrupt the receiver's state. | `fountain-codes` |\n262\t| D9 | **Display at ≤ half the *measured* camera fps** | PixNet's rule. Faster produces only torn frames. | `beyond-qr` |\n263\t| D10 | **Every frame DC-balanced** | Stops auto-exposure hunting; throughput swings 2.4× on exposure. Also part of the photosensitivity mitigation (§20.1). | `custom-codec` |\n264\t| D11 | **A runtime calibration probe decides luma-vs-colour, not this document** | Two research threads reached opposite conclusions (§6.6). The probe measures the device. | `beyond-qr` §6.6 |\n265\t| D12 | **Dark-on-light, not dual-polarity** | Dual-polarity costs ~50% throughput. OLED ABL means mostly-white loses ~4× brightness — \"light\" means *moderate*. | `pwa-platform` |\n266\t| D13 | **Add to Home Screen is mandatory on iOS** | Safari deletes service-worker caches after 7 days; Home Screen apps are exempt. | `pwa-platform` |\n267\t| D14 | **`exposureCompensation: min`; measure delivered fps, never trust `getSettings()`** | A precondition for D9. Android delivers 15 fps while reporting 30/60; the fix measured 15.0 → 41.6 fps. Absent on iOS — hence \"measured\". | `browser-qr-scanning` §1.4 |\n268\t| D15 | **Fragment length `L` is fixed for the session — not per profile, not ever** | Change L and K changes, invalidating every packet already collected. | `link-adaptation-design` |\n269\t| D16 | **Sender mixes 2–4 robustness profiles *within every frame*; no negotiation in v1** | Packets are fungible, so the sender never has to choose. **Probing is free** — a probe tile that succeeds delivers real payload. Mixed within a frame so profiles cannot alias against camera fps. | `link-adaptation` |\n270\t| D17 | **Conservative beacon profile, re-emitted periodically** | WiFi's lowest basic rate. Enables late join and re-acquisition. Carries all file metadata (D21). | `link-adaptation-design` |\n271\t| D18a | **Phase 3: the ladder runs at FIXED weights. No control loop.** | OLLA is closed-loop and its error signal (`cameraPxPerModule`) is a **receiver-side** metric, but only the sender can change rungs and D16 says no negotiation in v1. A controller with no observable cannot run. The research places fixed-weight ladders at T2/Phase 3 and weight adaptation at T4/Phase 5; an earlier revision collapsed the two. **Fixed weights (frame-area fractions): R1 (conservative v10-L) = 15%, R2 (nominal v15-L) = 60%, R3 (aggressive v20-L) = 25%. Never drop any rung below 10% in steady state.** | `link-adaptation` §10.2 |\n272\t| D18b | **Phase 5: adapt ladder weights from LOCAL metrics only — OLLA structure, 1:9 up/down asymmetry, ~1 s window, 2 s dwell, immediate hard step-down** | Closed-loop density control oscillates; profile selection stays a **stateless lookup** so there is no state machine to get stuck in. \"Local\" means the sender's own signals (frame timing, accelerometer à la COBRA), never receiver feedback. | `link-adaptation` §10.3 |\n273\t| D18c | **Assume 20–30% residual erasure. This is an ASSUMPTION about the channel, not a controlled target.** | Nothing in v1 observes erasure (D18a), so calling it a \"target\" was wrong. 20–30% is the evidence base's figure; driving it lower would mean the ladder is too conservative and throughput is being left unused. Dwell is sized to survive the **top** of the band (§8.1), and the repair code (§8.2) covers the tail beyond it. | `link-adaptation` §9.3 |\n274\t\n275\t---\n276\t\n277\t## 5. Invariants\n278\t\n279\tViolating one of these is a correctness bug, not a tuning choice. Each has an\n280\tenforcement mechanism, because an invariant nothing checks is a comment.\n281\t\n282\t| # | Invariant | Enforced by |\n283\t|---|---|---|\n284\t| **I1** | Fragment length **L** MUST NOT change within a session (D15) | Session type makes `L` `readonly`; property test asserts a mid-session change throws |\n285\t| **I2** | The degree distribution and the decoder MUST change together (D6); any distribution change MUST be simulated before merge | `sim/` assertions ported into the test suite; CI gate G4 |\n286\t| **I3** | Fountain indices MUST be derived from `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`, never transmitted (D7) | Golden test vector `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set`, bit-exact across implementations |\n287\t| **I4** | The file MUST NOT be fully materialised in memory on either side (D20) | Phase 1 flat-memory test over a synthetic 4 GB stream |\n288\t| **I5** | Exactly one block is GE-active at a time | Session type permits one `active`; assertion on block switch |\n289\t| **I6a** | **Block-layer** working set MUST stay ≤ 1 MB regardless of file size (264 KB at the adopted design) | A5 headless block-layer memory assertion |\n290\t| **I6b** | **Whole-receiver** peak MUST stay ≤ 64 MB, and the decode pool MUST hold ≤ 4 in-flight `VideoFrame`s | Phase 3 instrumented run. A single 1080p RGBA frame is **7.9 MiB**, so this budget is dominated by the camera path, not the codec — which is why I6 had to be split |\n291\t| **I7** | Frames MUST be generated on demand, never pre-rendered (D24) | Ring buffer is bounded at 3; assertion on buffer depth |\n292\t| **I8** | A packet failing `fcrc` or `streamId` MUST be discarded, never applied | Unit test with corrupted and foreign packets |\n293\t| **I9** | A block MUST NOT be written to OPFS until its hash verifies | Test: tamper a block, assert refusal + E-BLOCK-HASH |\n294\t| **I10** | Decoded output MUST be byte-identical to input | End-to-end property test, every phase |\n295\t\n296\t---\n297\t\n298\t## 6. Architecture\n299\t\n300\t### 6.1 Layering\n301\t\n302\t**Modulation is swappable**, and **the block layer bounds everything below it**.\n303\t\n304\t```\n305\t┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n306\t│ UI          role select · progress · file in/out · coach │\n307\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n308\t│ Session     metadata · compression · resume · verify     │\n309\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n310\t│ Block       file ⇄ 192 KB blocks · scheduling · bitmap   │\n311\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n312\t│ Fountain    LT encode (endless) / GF(2) GE decode        │\n313\t│             K = 768 · matrix 72.0 KB · CONSTANT          │\n314\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n315\t│ Framing     13-byte header + payload → packet bytes      │\n316\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n317\t│ Modulation  ◄──────────────────────── SWAPPABLE ────────►│\n318\t│   Stage 1   tiled monochrome QR                          │\n319\t│   Stage 2   + RGB channel tripling                       │\n320\t│   Stage 3   libcimbar-derived grid codec                 │\n321\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n322\t│ Transport   canvas render loop  /  camera capture loop   │\n323\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n324\t```\n325\t\n326\t```ts\n327\tinterface Modulation {\n328\t  readonly packetsPerFrame: number;     // 1 plain, ~15 tiled, ~45 tripled\n329\t  readonly bytesPerPacket: number;      // = 13 + L\n330\t  encodeFrame(packets: Uint8Array[]): ImageData;\n331\t  decodeFrame(frame: VideoFrame): Uint8Array[];   // 0..n — never throws\n332\t}\n333\t```\n334\t\n335\t`decodeFrame` returning fewer packets than `packetsPerFrame` is the **normal case**.\n336\tNothing above this layer may care.\n337\t\n338\t### 6.2 Threads and ownership\n339\t\n340\tLayer boundaries and thread boundaries are **not** the same, which is worth stating\n341\texplicitly because it is a common source of bugs:\n342\t\n343\t| Component | Thread | Owns |\n344\t|---|---|---|\n345\t| UI, canvas paint | main | display |\n346\t| Frame encoder | worker | ring buffer (depth 3, I7) |\n347\t| QR decode pool | N workers | `VideoFrame` — MUST `close()` each or the pipeline stalls |\n348\t| GE decoder | 1 worker | the 72 KB matrix; single-owner, no sharing |\n349\t| OPFS writer | worker | `createSyncAccessHandle` is worker-only |\n350\t\n351\t**Backpressure policy:** if decode falls behind capture, camera frames are **dropped, not\n352\tqueued**. A queued frame is stale by the time it decodes, and queuing turns a throughput\n353\tproblem into a memory problem. Dropped frames are erasures, which the fountain code\n354\talready absorbs.\n355\t\n356\t### 6.3 Sender pipeline\n357\t\n358\t```\n359\tFile ──► [sample: compressible?] ──► CompressionStream ──► OPFS staging\n360\t  │            (D8, skip if not)                              │\n361\t  └──────────────── or straight through ─────────────────────┘\n362\t                                                              │\n363\t                                   cut into 192 KB blocks (D19)\n364\t                                                              │\n365\t                 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n366\t                 ▼                                            ▼\n367\t        beacon (D17/D21) every ~2 s          per block: slice → K=768 fragments\n368\t        filename · size · blockCount           → LT encode (d ≤ 64, D25)\n369\t        blockSize · L · K · hash · flags       → header → tile\n370\t                 │                                            │\n371\t                 └──────────────► frame mixer ◄───────────────┘\n372\t                                       │\n373\t                          ladder of 2–4 profiles (D16)\n374\t                                       │\n375\t                              DC-balance (D10) ──► canvas\n376\t                                       │\n377\t                     display at ≤ ½ measured camera fps (D9/D14)\n378\t```\n379\t\n380\tThe sender **dwells** on each block (§8.1), then advances, looping the file\n381\tcontinuously. It never terminates on its own — it cannot know when the receiver is done.\n382\t\n383\t#### 6.3.1 Frames are generated on demand (D24)\n384\t\n385\tEvery arrow above is a **generator**, not an array.\n386\t\n387\t- **No finite frame set exists.** The LT encoder is rateless; how many frames a transfer\n388\t  needs depends on channel loss and is unknowable in advance.\n389\t- **One pass would not fit.** 4 GB ≈ 550,000 frames; as 1080p `ImageData` that is\n390\t  **4.2 TB**, ~55 GB even as PNGs.\n391\t- **On-demand is cheap.** ~0.29 ms per v15 tile (from 1.53 ms at v40, mask pinned) ×\n392\t  15 tiles × 15 fps ≈ **65 ms/sec, ~7% of one core**, plus ~2.3 ms/sec to render, plus\n393\t  **fountain XOR: 3.4 KB/packet at d ≤ 64 (D25) = 0.8 MB/s** at this geometry's\n394\t  **450 packets/s** (15 tiles × 2 packets/tile × 15 fps, using the R2 nominal rung) —\n395\t  negligible, but only because of the cap. Uncapped it is 6.1 MB/s\n396\t  at K = 768, and was 91.8 MB/s at the old K = 16,384.\n397\t\n398\tBecause indices derive from a PRNG (D7), the sender is **stateless**: frame *N* generates\n399\tdirectly without replaying 1…*N*−1. That is what makes resume and repair nearly free.\n400\t\n401\t**Implementation:** worker generator → ring buffer (depth 3) → main thread paints via\n402\t`rAF`. Deeper buffering is wasted memory (I7).\n403\t\n404\t#### 6.3.2 Shape the code region to the CAMERA, not the screen\n405\t\n406\tMeasured, and worth ~4–5× on its own. The receiver's camera has a fixed aspect and a fixed\n407\tpixel count; the sender's screen has a different one. What matters is **camera px per module**\n408\t(§2), and that is set by how much of the capture the code region fills.\n409\t\n410\tA 1920×1080 landscape code region imaged by a portrait 1080×1920 capture yields **M = 0.5625** —\n411\tso 4 screen px/module is only 2.25 camera px/module, below the cliff. Rendering the *same*\n412\tpayload into a **portrait-shaped region** inverts this:\n413\t\n414\t| Code region on screen | M | Camera px/module @ 2 screen px | Tiles | QR cap/frame | Payload/frame |\n415\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n416\t| 1920×1080 (naive: fill the screen) | 0.56 | 1.13 — **far below cliff** | 15 | 8.8 KB | 7.5 KB |\n417\t| 1080×1080 square | 1.00 | 2.00 — below cliff | 9 | 5.3 KB | 4.5 KB |\n418\t| **540×960 portrait** | **2.00** | **4.00 — above cliff** | 15 | **8.8 KB** | **7.5 KB** |\n419\t\n420\tSame tile count and same bytes per frame as the naive layout, but *above* the cliff instead of\n421\tbelow it — so yield goes from roughly a fifth to near-total. **The sender MUST size the code\n422\tregion to the receiver's capture aspect, not to its own display.** Since there is no\n423\tback-channel, it cannot know that aspect: expose it as a user-visible setting (portrait /\n424\tlandscape receiver) **defaulting to portrait, which is how phones are held — and portrait is\n425\ta fully supported mode, not a degraded one.** The 540×960 portrait region above clears the\n426\tcliff (4.00 camera px/module) at the *same* 7.5 KB/frame payload as the naive landscape\n427\tlayout. **Phase 3's ≥ 20 KB/s gate MUST pass with the receiver held portrait, unaided** —\n428\tthat is the default, unassisted case, not a stretch goal.\n429\t\n430\t**Packets-per-tile basis.** The R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 60% of tiles in steady state per D18a)\n431\tcarries **2 packets per tile**. Each packet is 269 B (13-byte header + 256 B payload), so\n432\t2 packets = 538 B per tile, which fits within v16-L's 586 B capacity. The **user-visible payload**\n433\tis 15 tiles × 2 packets/tile × 256 B = **7,680 B/frame ≈ 7.5 KB/frame**, matching the table\n434\tabove (per §13.2, all throughput figures quote user-visible bytes, not wire bytes). The **8.8 KB/frame\n435\tQR capacity** is 15 tiles × 586 B (v16-L capacity). At 15 fps, this geometry delivers\n436\t**7.5 KB × 15 fps = 112.5 KB/s payload rate** (or ~113 KB/s) before fountain overhead\n437\tand erasure loss.\n438\t\n439\t**Two routes to the same M; landscape is a free bonus, not a requirement.** Physically holding\n440\tthe receiver in landscape puts the screen's long axis on the camera's long axis — **1.78×,\n441\tfree, and it does not require halving screen px/module the way the portrait-region layout\n442\tdoes** — so it is worth *offering* to a user willing to turn the phone. But the app MUST NOT\n443\tdepend on the user doing so: the sender-side portrait region (above) is the primary,\n444\talways-on path, and landscape is strictly an optional upgrade for extra margin on top of it.\n445\t\n446\tVerified negative: forcing the receiver's *OS* orientation does not help — sensor mapping\n447\tfollows the device body, not the UI. Since portrait is the supported default, this mostly\n448\tdoesn't matter; it only matters for the optional landscape upgrade, which needs a *physical*\n449\tturn (§11 `E-ORIENTATION`, reframed below as a tip, not a requirement).\n450\t\n451\t### 6.4 Receiver pipeline\n452\t\n453\t```\n454\tgetUserMedia ──► exposureCompensation:min (D14) ──► measure real fps (rVFC, ~1 s)\n455\t      │\n456\t      └──► requestVideoFrameCallback ──► MediaStreamTrackProcessor*\n457\t                                                │\n458\t                              ROI crop (conditional — see §6.4)\n459\t                                                │\n460\t                              ┌─────────────────┴──── Worker pool ────┐\n461\t                              ▼                                       ▼\n462\t                      zxing readBarcodes                     [Stage 2: split\n463\t                      (all symbols, .bytes)                   R/G/B, stretch, ×3]\n464\t                              │\n465\t                    header parse ──► fcrc ──► streamId lock ──► route by blockIndex\n466\t                              │                                        │\n467\t                     beacon? ──┴──► learn size/blocks/K/hash    payload ──► GE decoder\n468\t                                    (gates everything)\n469\t                                                        rank == K ──► verify block hash\n470\t                                                                  ──► write to OPFS\n471\t                                                                  ──► mark bitmap, free\n472\t                                                                              │\n473\t                                            all blocks present ──► [decompress] ──► save\n474\t```\n475\t\n476\t\\* `MediaStreamTrackProcessor` is **Chromium-only**; `requestVideoFrameCallback` +\n477\t`drawImage` is the universal fallback and MUST be implemented (§16.3).\n478\t\n479\t**Block-layer working set: 264.0 KB** — 72.0 KB matrix + 192.0 KB block — flat regardless\n480\tof file size. This is *not* the whole-receiver figure; see I6a/I6b in §5.\n481\t\n482\tThree rules that are cheap to implement and expensive to omit:\n483\t\n484\t- **Measure fps, never trust it.** `getSettings()` reports 30/60 while the camera\n485\t  delivers 15.\n486\t- **Crop to ROI before decoding — but the 9× is conditional.** Measured 8.6× (56.9 → 6.6 ms)\n487\t  *when the code occupies part of the frame*. Once the grid fills the frame — which is what\n488\t  you want for camera px/module — **the ROI is the frame and the win evaporates** (69 ms).\n489\t  ROI is a recovery mechanism for being too far away, not a throughput optimisation at the\n490\t  right distance. **Except at high capture resolution**, where a tight quad-crop is what keeps\n491\t  camera px/module high *and* pixel count bounded at once — there it is load-bearing, and must\n492\t  be far tighter than the spike's 35%-margin version.\n493\t- **Select capture resolution deliberately — it is a first-class tunable.** Measured knee:\n494\t  720p → 100% erasure (1.5 camera px/module, nothing decodes); 1080p → best goodput; 4K →\n495\t  zero empty frames but 194 ms decode and 1.1 fps, net *worse*. Decode is O(pixels), so more\n496\t  resolution is not free. `getUserMedia` defaults are **not** adequate: a Pixel 6 defaults to\n497\t  1080 on the *short* edge.\n498\t- **Shape the code region to the camera, not the screen (sender-side, §6.3.2).**\n499\t- **Never offer a torch button.** It measured a 3.6× fps gain, which makes it tempting,\n500\t  but an LED on a glossy screen creates a specular hotspot that destroys a region of the\n501\t  frame. `exposureCompensation` gets the same mechanism without glare.\n502\t\n503\t### 6.5 Module layout and dependency pins\n504\t\n505\tCommitted in Phase 0 so \"where does this go?\" is not re-litigated eight phases running.\n506\tNote the layer boundaries of §6.1 and the thread boundaries of §6.2 are **not** the same,\n507\tso the tree separates them explicitly.\n508\t\n509\t```\n510\tsrc/\n511\t  core/                 # pure, no DOM, no workers — the testable heart\n512\t    fountain/           #   lt-encode.ts  ge-decode.ts  prng.ts  degree.ts\n513\t    block/              #   partition.ts  bitmap.ts  schedule.ts\n514\t    frame/              #   header.ts  beacon.ts  crc.ts  repair-code.ts\n515\t    hash/               #   block-hash.ts  stream-id.ts\n516\t  modulation/           # the swappable layer (§6.1)\n517\t    types.ts            #   the Modulation interface — the ONLY contract above\n518\t    qr-tiled/           #   stage 1: encode.ts  decode.ts  layout.ts  ladder.ts\n519\t    qr-colour/          #   stage 2\n520\t    grid/               #   stage 3\n521\t  workers/              # one file per thread role (§6.2)\n522\t    encode.worker.ts  decode.worker.ts  ge.worker.ts  opfs.worker.ts\n523\t  platform/             # every capability probe and fallback lives here\n524\t    camera.ts  storage.ts  wakelock.ts  share.ts  capabilities.ts\n525\t  ui/                   # role select, progress, coaching, pre-flight\n526\t  app.ts\n527\ttest/\n528\t  fixtures/             # conformance vectors (§14.3)\n529\t  degradation/          # synthetic blur/glare/tear generators\n530\tdocs/                   # plan, notes, research, sim\n531\t```\n532\t\n533\t**Rules.** `core/` MUST NOT import from `modulation/`, `workers/`, `platform/` or `ui/` —\n534\tit is the layer the property tests own. Nothing outside `modulation/` may reference QR\n535\t(D-modulation-swappable). Every browser capability check lives in\n536\t`platform/capabilities.ts`, never inline at a call site, so §16.1's platform matrix has\n537\texactly one implementation.\n538\t\n539\t**Dependency contract.** Exact-pinned, no ranges, no post-install scripts (gate G3).\n540\t\n541\t| Dependency | Pin | If unavailable |\n542\t|---|---|---|\n543\t| `zxing-wasm` | exact version + SRI on the `.wasm`. **MUST call `setZXingModuleOverrides({ locateFile })` pointing at a bundle-local, service-worker-precached `.wasm`.** See the warning below | Fatal on the receiver — surface `E-WASM-LOAD`; the sender still works |\n544\t| `node-qrcode` | exact version | Fatal on the sender; the receiver still works |\n545\t| `CompressionStream` | platform | Skip compression (D8 is already conditional) |\n546\t| `MediaStreamTrackProcessor` | platform | Fall back to `requestVideoFrameCallback` + `drawImage` — MUST be implemented, it is not Chromium-only |\n547\t| OPFS | platform | Refuse large files; cap at in-memory size and say so |\n548\t| Wake Lock | platform | Warn before a long transfer (`E-WAKELOCK-LOST`) |\n549\t\n550\t> ### ⚠️ `zxing-wasm` fetches its WASM from a CDN by default — this voids the entire premise\n551\t>\n552\t> Verified in the installed package: `dist/es/core-*.js` hard-codes\n553\t> `https://fastly.jsdelivr.net/npm/zxing-wasm@<ver>/dist/…` and fetches the `.wasm`\n554\t> **lazily on the first decode call**, not at page load. Shipping the default means the\n555\t> receiver:\n556\t>\n557\t> 1. makes a **third-party network request mid-session** — voiding T7, concept.md\n558\t>    constraint 1, and the README's \"provably no exfiltration\";\n559\t> 2. **fails completely in airplane mode** — i.e. in the flagship air-gapped use case (A8);\n560\t> 3. **executes remotely-fetched WASM** — precisely the supply-chain surface T5 exists for.\n561\t>\n562\t> The `.wasm` MUST be bundled, precached by the service worker, and located via\n563\t> `setZXingModuleOverrides`. §14.4's assertion covers this, and it is a **Phase 2 entry\n564\t> criterion** because Phase 2 is the first phase that loads a decoder.\n565\t\n566\t**Cross-origin isolation.** The pipeline uses transferable `VideoFrame`s and\n567\t`ArrayBuffer`s, **not** `SharedArrayBuffer` — so COOP/COEP headers are **not** required.\n568\tThis is deliberate: requiring them would constrain static hosting for no gain. Any future\n569\tuse of `SharedArrayBuffer` is a hosting decision, not just a code change.\n570\t\n571\t### 6.6 The luma-vs-colour disagreement, and how it is resolved\n572\t\n573\t| | `custom-codec-engineering.md` §7.2 | `beyond-qr-optical-channels.md` §6.6 |\n574\t|---|---|---|\n575\t| Colour cell penalty under 4:2:0 | 2× linear (4× area) — **derived** | 1.25× linear (1.56× area) — **measured** |\n576\t| Verdict | luma-only wins ~1.95× | RGB-tripling wins **1.98×** |\n577\t\n578\tThe measured result is better founded and the mechanism convincing: **chroma decimation\n579\tis a low-pass filter, not a deletion.** A binary chroma pattern at 5 px/module presents\n580\t2.5 chroma samples per module — above Nyquist; at 4 px/module exactly 2.0, right at\n581\tNyquist, which is where the measurement breaks. The \"2× per axis\" rule over-corrects by\n582\trestoring the *original* sampling density rather than staying above Nyquist in the\n583\tdecimated grid.\n584\t\n585\tAlso weighing against luma-only: 8-level luma measured **unusable** under handheld blur\n586\t(21.2% symbol error at 5 px/cell) vs **0.00%** for saturated 8-colour at 4 px/cell; and\n587\t**libcimbar spends 2 of its 6 bits per cell on colour**, with its deprecated 8-colour\n588\tmode benchmarking *faster*.\n589\t\n590\t**Resolution (D11): neither document decides.** A calibration probe measures the device\n591\tat session start. Where the luma-side note is unambiguously right: **AWB warps colour in\n592\tthree non-monotonic dimensions** and cannot be locked on iOS, so a per-frame in-band\n593\tcolour reference is **not optional** for Stage 2.\n594\t\n595\t---\n596\t\n597\t## 7. Data model\n598\t\n599\t### 7.1 Payload packet header — 13 bytes\n600\t\n601\t| Offset | Size | Field | Notes |\n602\t|---|---|---|---|\n603\t| 0 | 1 | `magic_ver` | 4-bit magic + 4-bit wire version. Rejects foreign QR instantly. See §16.3 for version skew. |\n604\t| 1 | 1 | `flags` | packet type (payload/beacon), reserved |\n605\t| 2 | 4 | `streamId` | Identifies the **file**. Seeds the PRNG; receiver locks it on first sight. Derivation: §7.4 |\n606\t| 6 | 3 | `blockIndex` | 16.7 M blocks × 192 KB = **3.0 TB** addressable — beyond any practical transfer (1 TB is 117 days) |\n607\t| 9 | 3 | `seq` | Sequence **within the block**; with `streamId`+`blockIndex` derives the index set |\n608\t| 12 | 1 | `fcrc` | CRC-8 — rejects a mis-decode before it poisons the matrix |\n609\t\n610\t`K`, `L` and the index set remain **derived, never transmitted** (I3).\n611\t\n612\t**`fcrc` covers bytes 0–11 only — the header, NOT the payload.** This is deliberate: CRC-8\n613\tover 269 bytes would be weak anyway, and the header is what must be trusted before a packet\n614\tis routed to a block. But the consequence must be stated plainly:\n615\t\n616\t> **A packet whose header is intact and whose 256-byte payload is corrupted passes `fcrc`\n617\t> unconditionally and poisons the GE matrix.** `fcrc` is a routing guard, not an integrity\n618\t> check.\n619\t\n620\tPayload integrity therefore rests on exactly two things: QR's own Reed–Solomon (which makes\n621\tan undetected symbol error rare, but not impossible) and **the per-block hash (§7.6), which\n622\tis the sole application-layer check on payload bytes.** That is why I9 is a MUST: a block\n623\tthat reaches rank K and fails its hash is discarded entirely and re-collected\n624\t(`E-BLOCK-HASH`, §11, E12). A test MUST corrupt a payload byte and assert the block hash\n625\tcatches it — corrupting only header bytes, as the current suite does, cannot detect this\n626\tclass at all.\n627\t\n628\t### 7.2 Beacon frame (D17/D21)\n629\t\n630\tEmitted every ~2 s at the most conservative profile. Everything the receiver needs before\n631\tit can interpret any payload packet:\n632\t\n633\t| Field | Size | Notes |\n634\t|---|---|---|\n635\t| `streamId` | 4 | Must match payload packets |\n636\t| `wireVersion` | 1 | Full version, not the 4-bit nibble |\n637\t| `fileSize` | 6 | 281 TB addressable — **MUST be bounds-checked** (§12, T1) |\n638\t| `blockSize`, `blockCount` | 3 + 3 | Yields K and the last block's short length |\n639\t| `fragmentLen` (L) | 2 | Fixed for the session (I1) |\n640\t| `degreeCap` | 1 | D25; receiver MUST use the same cap |\n641\t| `flags` | 1 | compressed / hash alg / colour profile |\n642\t| `blockHashLen` | 1 | Per-block hash truncation length |\n643\t| `wholeFileHash` | 32 | **Mandatory.** concept.md constraint 4 makes byte-exact reconstruction non-negotiable and names this as the verification. An earlier revision made it optional \"on very large files\" — i.e. dropped the guarantee exactly where E5 (source mutated during a 10-hour read) is most likely and the stakes are highest. Computed by streaming the reassembled file through an incremental WASM hasher (§3.3); the cost is one extra read, not one extra copy |\n644\t| `filename`, `mimeType` | var | Length-prefixed UTF-8, **sanitised** (§12, T2) |\n645\t\n646\tThe receiver shows \"acquiring…\" until its first beacon.\n647\t\n648\t### 7.6 The block-hash manifest — how per-block hashes reach the receiver\n649\t\n650\tI9, E12, §6.4, §8.3 and §7.4 all depend on per-block hashes, and §7.1 establishes they are\n651\tthe *only* application-layer check on payload bytes. Nothing in the wire format carried\n652\tthem: the 13-byte header has no room, and the beacon carries only `blockHashLen`.\n653\t\n654\t**A 4 GB file has 21,845 blocks. Even 4-byte hashes are 87 KB — far beyond a beacon.**\n655\t\n656\t**Resolution: hashes travel as a manifest, fountain-coded like any other block.**\n657\t\n658\t| Property | Value |\n659\t|---|---|\n660\t| Transport | A dedicated **manifest stream**, `blockIndex = 0xFFFFFF`, distinguished by `PacketFlags.Manifest` |\n661\t| Contents | `blockCount × blockHashLen` truncated hashes, in block order |\n662\t| `blockHashLen` | **4 bytes.** Per-block false accept 2⁻³², ~5×10⁻⁶ across 21,845 blocks — comfortably below the whole-file hash's job |\n663\t| Coding | Its own `K_manifest = ceil(blockCount × 4 / L)`, same LT encoder, same GE decoder |\n664\t| Cadence | Interleaved with payload on the same schedule as the beacon (D17), so a late joiner acquires it without waiting a pass |\n665\t| Before it arrives | Completed blocks are written to OPFS but **not marked in the bitmap**; they are verified retroactively once the manifest decodes. The receiver reports \"verifying…\" rather than claiming completion |\n666\t\n667\t**Why not append the hash to each block's payload:** it would make the payload\n668\t`blockSize + 4`, breaking `blockSize = K·L` and therefore D19's entire arithmetic and G7.\n669\t\n670\t**Sizing sanity:** 21,845 × 4 B = 87 KB ⇒ `K_manifest` = 342 fragments — one third of a\n671\tnormal block, decodable well inside the first pass.\n672\t\n673\t### 7.3 Session state\n674\t\n675\t```ts\n676\ttype SendSession = {\n677\t  source: File;\n678\t  staging: FileSystemFileHandle | null;   // compressed copy (D8) — MUST be wiped\n679\t  streamId: number;\n680\t  blockSize: number; blockCount: number;\n681\t  readonly fragmentLen: number;           // L — I1\n682\t  readonly K: number;                     // D26\n683\t  cursor: { blockIndex: number; seq: number };\n684\t  dwellPackets: number;                   // §8.1\n685\t};\n686\t\n687\ttype RecvSession = {\n688\t  streamId: number | null;                // locked on first valid header\n689\t  meta: BeaconMeta | null;                // gates everything\n690\t  complete: Uint8Array;                   // block bitmap — the resume token\n691\t  active: { blockIndex: number; pivots: Map<number, GERow>; rank: number } | null;  // I5\n692\t  out: FileSystemWritableFileStream;      // OPFS\n693\t  stats: { fps: number; cameraPxPerModule: number; packetsPerSec: number; eta: number };\n694\t};\n695\t```\n696\t\n697\tPartial state for a block the sender has moved past is **discarded, not persisted** — a\n698\tbadly damaged block rarely half-completes usefully, and persisting it would defeat I6.\n699\tThe bitmap is tiny: 4 GB / 192 KB = 21,845 blocks = **2.7 KB**.\n700\t\n701\t### 7.4 `streamId` derivation\n702\t\n703\tLoad-bearing: D22 resume requires that re-selecting the same file reproduces the same\n704\t`streamId`, and §3.3 says a full multi-GB hash is not free.\n705\t\n706\t**Derivation (sender):**\n707\t\n708\t```\n709\tstreamId = CRC32( fileSize ‖ first 64 KB ‖ middle 64 KB ‖ last 64 KB ‖ lastModified )\n710\t```\n711\t\n712\tThree sampled windows plus size and mtime. Costs ~200 KB of reads regardless of file\n713\tsize, so it is instant even for 4 TB.\n714\t\n715\t**What this buys and what it does not:**\n716\t\n717\t- ✅ Same file re-selected → same `streamId` → resume works.\n718\t- ✅ Different files → different `streamId` with overwhelming probability.\n719\t- ⚠️ A file edited **only in the middle**, keeping size and mtime, collides. Mitigated by\n720\t  including `lastModified`, and by per-block hashes catching the mismatch at block level.\n721\t- ⚠️ This is **not** a content-integrity hash. The whole-file hash (§7.2) is, and is\n722\t  optional. `streamId` is an *identifier*.\n723\t\n724\tDeliberately **not** `crc32(payload)` — the research's original design — because the\n725\tblock layer made a full-payload pass unaffordable.\n726\t\n727\t### 7.5 Repair code format (§8.2)\n728\t\n729\tA human types this, so it must be short, unambiguous, and self-checking.\n730\t\n731\t```\n732\tSF1-<streamId36>-<ranges36>-<check>\n733\t```\n734\t\n735\t- **Alphabet:** Crockford base32 (no I/L/O/U — removes the common misreadings).\n736\t- **`ranges`:** run-length encoded missing-block set. Contiguous runs are the common case\n737\t  because misses cluster (the user looked away).\n738\t- **`check`:** 2 characters, CRC-8 over the decoded body. A mistyped code MUST be\n739\t  rejected, never acted on — acting on a corrupted range wastes hours.\n740\t- **Length bound:** if the encoded form exceeds **48 characters**, the receiver MUST\n741\t  instead offer a QR containing the same payload (which the sender's camera reads, or the\n742\t  user photographs), and say so. A 100 GB file with scattered misses can exceed any\n743\t  reasonable typing length, and silently truncating the set would be a correctness bug.\n744\t\n745\t---\n746\t\n747\t## 8. Behaviour at gigabyte scale\n748\t\n749\t### 8.1 Block scheduling and the dwell budget\n750\t\n751\tThe sender does not know which blocks the receiver has, so it dwells on each block for\n752\t`dwellPackets`, then advances, looping the file continuously.\n753\t\n754\t**Dwell must survive the top of the assumed erasure band.** An earlier revision paired\n755\tdwell 1.4 K with a 20–30% band, which failed at the top of its own band — at 30%\n756\terasure, 1.4 K delivers 0.98 K against the ~1.02 K needed, so **every block missed its\n757\tfirst pass**, each costing a full extra pass.\n758\t\n759\tThe fix is to raise dwell, **not** to narrow the band. Narrowing it (a briefly-adopted\n760\tmistake) contradicts the evidence base, which specifies 20–30% and warns that driving\n761\terasure lower means the ladder is too conservative and throughput is being left unused.\n762\t\n763\t| dwell | 20% erasure | 25% | **30%** | needed |\n764\t|---|---|---|---|---|\n765\t| 1.4 K | 1.120 K | 1.050 K | **0.980 K ❌** | ~1.02 K |\n766\t| **1.6 K** | 1.280 K | 1.200 K | **1.120 K ✅** | ~1.02 K |\n767\t\n768\t- **dwell = 1.6 × K** (default; tunable)\n769\t- **assumed band = 20–30%** (D18c) — an assumption, not a controlled target\n770\t\n771\tA test MUST assert `dwell × (1 − erasure_max) ≥ 1.12`, matching §13.1's +12% p99\n772\toverhead budget, so dwell and the band cannot drift apart again.\n773\t\n774\t**When real erasure exceeds 30%** — which nothing in v1 can detect (D18a) — blocks miss\n775\tand the **repair code (§8.2) is the recovery path**, not a tighter loop. This is the\n776\tdesigned answer, not a gap.\n777\t\n778\t**Dwell is a standing ~60% overhead.** The sender always emits 1.6× what a block needs,\n779\twhatever the channel. §13.1's throughput budgets are stated **after** this factor —\n780\tthey are goodput, not wire rate.\n781\t\n782\t### 8.2 Human-mediated repair — the cheap back-channel\n783\t\n784\tThe receiver knows exactly which blocks it lacks. The user reads a code off one screen and\n785\ttypes it into the other:\n786\t\n787\t> **Receiver:** \"Missing 3 blocks. Repair code: `SF1-K7F2M9-3B-X4`\"\n788\t> **Sender:** [paste] → transmits only those blocks\n789\t\n790\tTurns a multi-hour extra pass into a sub-minute repair, needs no second camera and no\n791\tgeometry constraints, and is what makes small blocks (§3.4) affordable. Format: §7.5.\n792\t\n793\t### 8.3 Resume (D22)\n794\t\n795\tThe receiver persists `{streamId, meta, bitmap}` plus the OPFS output after every completed\n796\tblock. On reload it offers to resume. At 2.7 KB per 4 GB this is nearly free.\n797\t\n798\tThe sender is stateless across restarts by construction (D24) **when compression is disabled** —\n799\tit needs only the same file and the same `streamId` (§7.4). **With compression enabled, resume is\n800\tNOT supported** — see `notes/bf-17s0-resume-compression-conflict.md` for the full analysis.\n801\tThe short version: `CompressionStream` offers no determinism guarantee, so re-compression after\n802\tstaging is reaped (E11) would produce different blocks and silently corrupt the receiver's state.\n803\tThe beacon carries a `RESUME_DISABLED` flag when compression is on; the receiver uses it to\n804\tsuppress the resume UI.\n805\t\n806\t**On resume the receiver MUST re-verify block hashes** rather than trusting the bitmap, in\n807\tcase OPFS was corrupted or the file was touched externally.\n808\t\n809\t### 8.4 Storage limits\n810\t\n811\t| Platform | Practical quota |\n812\t|---|---|\n813\t| Chrome / Edge desktop | ~60% of free disk — multi-GB fine |\n814\t| Firefox | ~10% of disk (capped ~10 GB) |\n815\t| **Safari / iOS** | **~1 GB** before prompting; expandable but user-gated |\n816\t\n817\t**Multi-GB reception is a desktop-Chromium story.** The app MUST query\n818\t`navigator.storage.estimate()` up front and refuse clearly (§13.1) rather than failing at\n819\thour 9. With compression on, staging needs the compressed size *plus* the output.\n820\t\n821\t---\n822\t\n823\t## 9. Acceptance scenarios\n824\t\n825\tNamed, independently verifiable, with explicit pass **and fail** criteria. \"Fail\" means\n826\tstop and reconsider the design, not retry.\n827\t\n828\t| # | Scenario | Setup | Action | Pass | Fail |\n829\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n830\t| **A1** | Small file, ideal conditions | Laptop (1080p, 50% brightness min) → Pixel-class phone, 30 cm, office lighting (~300 lux), tripod | Send a 1 MB binary file (random bytes, incompressible) | Byte-identical output; ≥ 20 KB/s sustained; completes in ≤ 60 s | < 10 KB/s, or any byte differs |\n831\t| **A1-lite** | Byte-exactness on two real devices | Two real devices (any configuration) | Send any file | Byte-identical output | Any byte differs |\n832\t| **A2** | Handheld, realistic | As A1 but handheld, receiver held **portrait** (the default, unassisted grip — §6.3.2) | Send 1 MB | Byte-identical; ≥ 10 KB/s | Does not complete in 5 min |\n833\t| **A3** | Phone → phone | Two phones, 15 cm, handheld | Send 100 KB | Byte-identical; completes in ≤ 5 min | Does not complete — triggers §18 R4 |\n834\t| **A4** | Lossy channel | A1 setup; camera deliberately occluded 30% of the time in 2-second bursts | Send 1 MB | Byte-identical; ≤ 1.6× the A1 frame count | > 3× A1 frame count (fountain code is not delivering) |\n835\t| **A5** | Large file, memory flat | Desktop Chromium, synthetic 4 GB stream, headless block layer | Full encode→decode at the block layer | Byte-identical; peak heap ≤ 1 MB (I6a); no growth trend across 21,800 blocks | Any monotonic memory growth |\n836\t| **A6** | Resume | A1 setup, 10 MB file | Reload the receiver tab at ~50% | Offers resume; completes; byte-identical | Restarts from zero, or completes with wrong bytes |\n837\t| **A7** | Repair | A1 setup, 10 MB file, 5 blocks deliberately dropped | Enter the repair code on the sender | Only the missing blocks retransmit; completes in < 60 s | Full pass required |\n838\t| **A8** | Offline | Both devices in airplane mode, app previously loaded | Full A1 transfer | Completes normally | Any network request attempted (asserted by CI, §14.4) |\n839\t| **A9** | Wrong stream | Two senders visible in frame | Receiver points at both | Locks one `streamId`, ignores the other, says so | Mixes packets from both |\n840\t| **A10** | Hostile beacon | Crafted beacon declaring `fileSize` = 281 TB | Receiver parses it | Refuses with `E-META-BOUNDS`; no allocation attempted | Allocates or crashes |\n841\t\n842\t**Adoption metrics are deliberately absent.** With no backend and no telemetry there is no\n843\tway to measure them, and the ledger consciously cut the voluntary-benchmark idea. This is a\n844\tstated limitation, not an oversight — see §18 R8.\n845\t\n846\t---\n847\t\n848\t## 10. Edge case catalog\n849\t\n850\t| # | Case | Resolution |\n851\t|---|---|---|\n852\t| E1 | **Zero-byte file** | Reject at selection with a clear message. `K = 0` is undefined. |\n853\t| E2 | **File smaller than one fragment** (< 256 B) | Pad to one fragment; `K = 1`; the fountain code degenerates to repetition, which is correct. Research specifies a `K < 8` guard — adopt it: below 8 fragments, send plain repetition, no LT. Signalled by a `flags` bit in the beacon so the receiver selects the same path. |\n854\t| E3a | **The last block is short** — its K is `ceil(lastLen / L)`, not 768. Both sides derive K per block, and D7's PRNG is seeded with it. A mismatch produces wrong index sets, so the block never decodes and nothing says why. | Derive per-block K from `(blockIndex, blockSize, fileSize)` in **one shared function** used by both encoder and decoder; conformance vector covers the last block explicitly. |\n855\t| E3b | **`blockCount == 1`** | Normal path; no special case, but tested explicitly since off-by-one in block iteration is likely. |\n856\t| E4 | **Incompressible input where deflate expands it** | D8 samples first; if the sample ratio > 0.92, skip compression. If compression still expands, discard the staging file and send raw. |\n857\t| E5 | **Source file changes mid-transfer** | A 10-hour read of a live `File` handle is the *normal* case. Re-check `file.size` and `lastModified` before each block read; on mismatch abort with `E-SOURCE-CHANGED`. Emitting blocks from two versions would produce a file that passes per-block hashes and fails the whole-file hash after hours. |\n858\t| E6 | **Duplicate packet arrives** | GE reduces it to a zero row; contributes nothing, costs one reduction. No special handling. |\n859\t| E7 | **Two senders in frame** | `streamId` lock (A9); packets from the unlocked stream are discarded and surfaced as `E-FOREIGN-STREAM`. |\n860\t| E8 | **Tab backgrounded on the sender** | `rAF` stops in a background tab, so a 10-hour transfer silently halts. Wake Lock does **not** cover this. Detect via `visibilitychange` and warn loudly; the transfer is paused, not failed. |\n861\t| E9 | **Camera permission revoked mid-run** | Pause, preserve the bitmap, prompt for re-grant. Never discard collected blocks. |\n862\t| E10 | **OPFS quota exhausted mid-transfer** | Stop, keep completed blocks, export a partial file plus a manifest of what is missing. Never silently truncate. **The kept partial artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n863\t| E11 | **Abandoned staging file** | Sender-side staging keyed by `streamId`; on startup, reap staging files with no active session. Also a privacy requirement (§12, T4a). |\n864\t| E12 | **Block reaches rank K but fails its hash** | Discard the whole block, clear its bitmap bit, re-collect. Emit `E-BLOCK-HASH`. This is the CRC-8 false-accept path (§7.1) and MUST be implemented — at GB scale a silent re-do costs hours. |\n865\t| E13 | **Whole-file hash fails after all blocks pass** | Indicates E5 or a block-hash collision. Report `E-FILE-HASH`; keep the output and label it unverified rather than deleting hours of work. |\n866\t| E14 | **Filename with path separators or control bytes** | Sanitise on export (§12, T2). Never write an attacker-chosen path. |\n867\t| E15 | **Decompression fails at the end** | All blocks verified but the gzip stream is invalid → `E-DECOMPRESS`; keep the compressed artefact so nothing is lost. **The kept artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n868\t| E16 | **Worker crash mid-block** | Restart the worker, discard the active block only, keep the bitmap. |\n869\t| E17a | **Sender-side thermal throttling** | Observed: the bench laptop decayed 6.7 → 2.4 fps over two minutes. Locally observable, so D18b's local step-down applies. |\n870\t| E17b | **Receiver-side thermal throttling** | Observed at **70 °C / throttling threshold within 20–30 minutes**. D18a's rule bites: fps decline is a *receiver* observation, the ladder is a *sender* control, and there is no back-channel — so \"step the ladder down\" is **structurally impossible** here. Mitigate locally instead: **duty-cycle (D27)** and drop decode resolution. |\n871\t| E18 | **Resume offered for a file the user no longer has** (sender side) | `streamId` mismatch on re-selection → offer a fresh transfer, do not silently restart. |\n872\t\n873\t---\n874\t\n875\t## 11. Error taxonomy\n876\t\n877\tEvery distinguishable condition gets a stable code and one user-facing sentence. Defined\n878\tnow, before Phase 5 designs any UI — after that, taxonomies get retrofitted to screens.\n879\t\n880\t**Optical / acquisition** (the stall detector's job, `bf-5vm`):\n881\t\n882\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n883\t|---|---|---|\n884\t| `E-NO-SIGNAL` | No decodable tiles at all | \"Point the camera at the sending screen.\" |\n885\t| `E-TOO-FAR` | **camera** px/module < 4 (§2) | \"Move closer — the code is too small to read.\" |\n886\t| `E-TOO-CLOSE` | Symbol exceeds frame, or below min focus | \"Move back a little.\" |\n887\t| `E-BLUR` | Sharpness metric below threshold | \"Hold steady.\" |\n888\t| `E-DARK` | Insufficient exposure | \"Too dark — raise the sender's screen brightness.\" |\n889\t| `E-GLARE` | Saturated region over the code | \"Tilt to avoid the reflection.\" |\n890\t| `E-FOCUS-HUNT` | Focus oscillating | \"Tap the screen to lock focus.\" |\n891\t| `E-ORIENTATION` | Detected capture aspect doesn't match the sender's configured setting (§6.3.2) — e.g. sender is shaping the code for landscape but the receiver is held portrait | \"This app works fine held normally — but if you'd like more margin, match the orientation setting on the sending device, or turn the phone sideways.\" (tip, not a blocker — portrait is fully supported) |\n892\t| `E-SENDER-STALLED` | Identical frames repeating | \"The sending device seems paused.\" |\n893\t| `E-TORN` | Torn-frame rate high | \"Lower the sender's frame rate.\" |\n894\t\n895\t**Protocol:**\n896\t\n897\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n898\t|---|---|---|---|\n899\t| `E-FOREIGN-STREAM` | Different `streamId` (E7) | \"That's a different file — ignoring it.\" | automatic, informational |\n900\t| `E-VERSION` | Unknown `magic_ver` (§16.3) | \"The sending device is running version X; this one is Y. Update both.\" | user must update |\n901\t| `E-META-BOUNDS` | Beacon field out of bounds (T1) | \"That transmission looks malformed and was rejected.\" | automatic, refuse |\n902\t| `E-BLOCK-HASH` | Rank K reached, hash failed (E12) | \"A chunk arrived corrupted and is being re-collected.\" | automatic retry |\n903\t| `E-FILE-HASH` | Whole-file hash failed (E13) | \"The file is complete but failed its final check — saved as unverified.\" | keep output, warn |\n904\t| `E-REPAIR-CODE` | Repair code checksum failed | \"That repair code doesn't look right — check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n905\t| `E-WASM-LOAD` | Decoder failed to load | \"The scanner failed to start. Reload the page.\" | user reloads |\n906\t\n907\t**Local / resource:**\n908\t\n909\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n910\t|---|---|---|---|\n911\t| `E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT` | Not enough storage (§13.1) | \"Not enough free space: this needs X, you have Y.\" | user frees space |\n912\t| `E-QUOTA-EXHAUSTED` | Ran out mid-transfer (E10) | \"Out of space. Saved what arrived — X of Y chunks.\" | partial export |\n913\t| `E-SOURCE-CHANGED` | Source mutated (E5) | \"The file changed while sending. Start again to avoid a corrupt copy.\" | restart required |\n914\t| `E-BACKGROUNDED` | Sender tab backgrounded (E8) | \"Sending paused — keep this tab visible.\" | auto-resume on focus |\n915\t| `E-CAMERA-LOST` | Permission revoked (E9) | \"Camera access ended. Your progress is saved.\" | re-grant, resume |\n916\t| `E-WAKELOCK-LOST` | Screen may sleep | \"The screen may turn off. Adjust your sleep settings.\" | user acts |\n917\t| `E-DECOMPRESS` | Decompression failed (E15) | \"Everything arrived but couldn't be unpacked. The raw data was kept.\" | keep artefact |\n918\t\n919\t---\n920\t\n921\t## 12. Threat model\n922\t\n923\tThe README claims \"provably no exfiltration\" and \"auditable once and trusted thereafter\".\n924\tThat claim needs backing. In scope for v1:\n925\t\n926\t| # | Threat | Stance | Test |\n927\t|---|---|---|---|\n928\t| **T1** | **Crafted optical stream — resource exhaustion.** Beacon-declared `fileSize` (281 TB), `blockCount` (16.7 M) and `L` are attacker-controlled and size allocations. | **Mitigated.** Bounds-check every beacon field before use: `L` ∈ [1, 4096], `K` ≤ locally benchmarked max (D26), `blockCount` ≤ 16.7 M, `fileSize` ≤ available quota. Reject with `E-META-BOUNDS`. Never allocate from a declared size. | A10 + fuzz beacon fields |\n929\t| **T2** | **Path traversal / hostile filename.** `filename` is attacker-supplied and reaches a save dialog. | **Mitigated.** Strip path separators, control bytes and leading dots; cap length; never pass through unsanitised. | unit: filenames with `../`, NUL, control bytes |\n930\t| **T3** | **Decompression bomb.** The receiver decompresses attacker-supplied data. | **Mitigated.** Enforce a max expansion ratio (100:1) and an absolute cap = declared `fileSize`; abort with `E-DECOMPRESS` on overrun. | unit: 1 GB-expanding zip bomb → `E-DECOMPRESS` |\n931\t| **T4a** | **Sender-side plaintext residue.** D8 writes a *decompressed-equivalent* copy of the user's file to OPFS as staging. For the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) this is real exposure. | **Mitigated.** Wipe staging on completion, on cancel, and on startup-reap (E11). Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest and the OS/browser may retain it. | integration: assert sender OPFS empty after complete/cancel/reap |\n932\t| **T4b** | **Receiver-side plaintext residue.** The receiver stages the complete decoded file in OPFS. The output **is** the deliverable — it cannot be deleted immediately. For sensitive files (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) indefinite storage is exposure. | **Mitigated.** Implement a deletion lifecycle: (1) delete after successful `share()`/`save()`; (2) reap orphaned outputs on startup; (3) warn before keeping partial artefacts (E10, E15); (4) provide a user-visible delete control. Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest. | integration: assert receiver OPFS empty after successful save; reap deletes orphans; UI has delete control; warning shown for partial artefacts |\n933\t| **T5** | **Supply chain.** The security claim depends on the bundle being what was audited. | **Partially mitigated.** `bf-13h` covers the output half (version footer + published hash). The input half — pinned dependency versions, WASM integrity, no post-install scripts — is a Phase 0 requirement (§14.5). | G3: lockfile diff + SRI check in CI |\n934\t| **T6** | **Shoulder-surfing / filming.** The optical channel is uniquely exposed: anyone with a camera in the room captures the same stream. | **Accepted for v1, consciously.** concept.md scopes encryption as a non-goal; §19 Q10 keeps it live. The app MUST NOT claim confidentiality it does not provide — the UI should say the transmission is visible to anyone who can see the screen. | none — accepted, not mitigated |\n935\t| **T7** | **No telemetry, by construction.** | **Committed.** The app makes **zero** network requests after load. Enforced by CI (§14.4) and by A8. This is a stronger and more checkable claim than a privacy policy. | §14.4 network assertion + A8 |\n936\t\n937\t**Out of scope for v1, stated:** authenticating the *sender* (no PKI, no trust anchor); a\n938\tmalicious *receiver* (it only gets what it is shown); side-channels other than the optical\n939\tone; physical device compromise.\n940\t\n941\t---\n942\t\n943\t## 13. Performance budgets and benchmark contract\n944\t\n945\t### 13.1 Budgets — committed, not forecast\n946\t\n947\t§15's table is *expectation*. These are the numbers the build is held to.\n948\t\n949\t**Throughput basis.** All throughput budgets are **user-visible file bytes per second** after:\n950\t- Fountain coding overhead (+12% p99 at K=768 with D25's cap)\n951\t- Erasure loss (20–30% assumed band per D18c)\n952\t- Dwell overhead (60% standing overhead per §8.1)\n953\t\n954\tThe gross wire rate at the R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps) is\n955\t**112.5 KB/s payload** (7.5 KB/frame × 15 fps). After fountain (+12%) and 30% erasure,\n956\tnet goodput is **~70 KB/s** — well above the 20 KB/s budget.\n957\t\n958\t| Budget | Value | Gate |\n959\t|---|---|---|\n960\t| Throughput, A1 reference setup | **≥ 20 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3 |\n961\t| Throughput, A3 phone→phone | **≥ 3 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3; miss triggers §18 R4 |\n962\t| Block-layer working set | **≤ 1 MB**, any file size (I6a) | Phase 1 |\n963\t| Whole-receiver peak | **≤ 64 MB**, ≤ 4 in-flight `VideoFrame`s (I6b) | Phase 3 |\n964\t| GE sustained XOR need | **≤ 200 MB/s** at the fastest supported stage (modelled 114.6 MB/s, 1.74× margin) — **measured 3,260 MB/s desktop / ~815 MB/s est. phone; the budget was ~16× pessimistic.** R1 provisionally closed, pending an on-device run *while thermally throttled* | Phase 1 + G7 |\n965\t| Per-camera-frame decode | **≤ 60 ms** p99 (leaves headroom at 15 fps) — **measured 67–69 ms p50 full-frame, 194 ms at 4K, 6.6 ms with a tight ROI. p50 already exceeds the p99 budget**; the fixes (worker pool §6.2, tight ROI §6.4) are unimplemented, so this is violated by the instrument, not yet by the design | Phase 3 |\n966\t| Encode + render per frame | **≤ 20 ms** p99 — **measured ~150 ms** (6.7 fps against 12 requested) on a 2015 laptop with D4's pinned mask unimplemented | Phase 3 |\n967\t| Time-to-first-packet after aim | **≤ 3 s** p50 | Phase 5 |\n968\t| Reception overhead vs K | **≤ +5%** mean, **≤ +12%** p99 (measured: +2.97% / +4.2%) | Phase 1, `sim/` |\n969\t| **Warn threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 30 min** → explicit confirm | Phase 4 |\n970\t| **Refuse threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 24 h**, or quota insufficient → refuse with an override | Phase 4 |\n971\t\n972\t### 13.2 Benchmark denominator — the contract\n973\t\n974\tEvery throughput number in this repo MUST state all of these, or it is not a measurement:\n975\t\n976\t| Parameter | Reference value |\n977\t|---|---|\n978\t| **Unit** | **User-visible file bytes per second.** Not wire bytes. With compression these differ 3–10×. |\n979\t| Sender | 1080p display, 50%+ brightness, DC-balanced frames |\n980\t| Receiver | Mid-range Android (Pixel-6-class), rear camera |\n981\t| Distance | 30 cm (laptop→phone), 15 cm (phone→phone) |\n982\t| Mounting | Tripod for budget figures; handheld reported separately, never mixed |\n983\t| Lighting | ~300 lux, no direct glare |\n984\t| File | 1 MB of random bytes (incompressible) unless stated |\n985\t| Duration | ≥ 60 s sustained; startup excluded |\n986\t| Trials | ≥ 5; report median and p99, never the best run |\n987\t\n988\t**§15's comparison table mixes measurement regimes** — PixNet's 12 Mb/s used a 30\" LCD and\n989\ta 24 MP DSLR. Such figures MUST be labelled with their regime and never compared directly\n990\tto handheld numbers.\n991\t\n992\t---\n993\t\n994\t## 14. Testing strategy and quality gates\n995\t\n996\t### 14.1 Tiers\n997\t\n998\t| Tier | What | Runs |\n999\t|---|---|---|\n1000\t| **T-unit** | Codec internals, header parse, CRC, bitmap, repair-code round-trip | Every commit |\n1001\t| **T-property** | Random files × random loss patterns → byte-exact; overhead within simulation bounds | Every commit |\n1002\t| **T-stub-camera** | `getUserMedia` stubbed with `canvas.captureStream(0)` + `requestFrame()`. No flags, frame-exact, deterministic | Every commit |\n1003\t| **T-degradation** | Synthetic blur / rotation / keystone / glare / rolling-shutter tearing applied to rendered frames. **Assert decode *rates*, not booleans** | Nightly |\n1004\t| **T-real-capture** | Frames → Y4M → Chromium fake camera. Proven in research (byte-exact, including late-join at 700 ms) | Nightly |\n1005\t| **T-scale** | Synthetic 4 GB stream at the block layer; assert flat memory across 21,800 blocks | Nightly |\n1006\t| **T-physical-rig** | Two real devices, fixed mounting, the §13.2 denominator. **This is the acceptance gate for §13.1 throughput** — nothing else can measure it | Per release |\n1007\t| **T-manual-iOS** | Full pass on a real iPhone. **Not CI-testable at any price** — WebKit cannot fake a camera, the Simulator has none | Per release |\n1008\t\n1009\t> **Trap, already paid for:** `--use-fake-device-for-media-capture` **does not exist**. It\n1010\t> is `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, and the file flag requires it.\n1011\t\n1012\t### 14.2 Binary-safety testing\n1013\t\n1014\t**MUST use real compressed payloads at several lengths — never ASCII.** Corruption in the\n1015\trejected libraries was both *content*- and *length*-dependent: the same generator\n1016\tround-tripped at 600 bytes and corrupted at 256. An ASCII suite marks every library safe,\n1017\tincluding the broken ones. The nastiest case, `@zxing/library.getText()`, returns the\n1018\t**correct length** while collapsing bytes ≥ 0x80 to U+FFFD — a length assertion passes and\n1019\tthe file is silently ruined. Assert on bytes, at multiple lengths, over 0x00–0xFF.\n1020\t\n1021\t### 14.3 Conformance vectors\n1022\t\n1023\tShip as fixtures, because they are what a third-party implementation would need:\n1024\t\n1025\t- `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set` — bit-exact, pinning the PRNG (I3)\n1026\t- Header encode/decode round-trip at every field boundary\n1027\t- Beacon encode/decode including absent optional fields\n1028\t- Repair-code round-trip, including a deliberately mistyped code\n1029\t- A **two-realm test**: the same built app in two contexts, one sending, one receiving —\n1030\t  the only test that actually verifies the \"both roles, one page\" constraint\n1031\t\n1032\t### 14.4 The no-network assertion\n1033\t\n1034\tCI MUST fail the build if the running app issues **any** network request after load —\n1035\tincluding the lazy WASM fetch described in §6.5, which is the most likely violation and\n1036\tdoes not occur until the first decode, so **the assertion must exercise a decode**\n1037\t(intercept `fetch`/`XHR`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource`/`Image`; fail on any call). This is the\n1038\texecutable form of T7 and of concept.md constraint 1.\n1039\t\n1040\t### 14.5 Quality gates\n1041\t\n1042\t| Gate | Requirement |\n1043\t|---|---|\n1044\t| **G1** | Typecheck, lint, unit, property, stub-camera all green |\n1045\t| **G2** | No network requests (§14.4) |\n1046\t| **G3** | Bundle-size budget not exceeded; dependencies pinned to exact versions, no post-install scripts (T5) |\n1047\t| **G4** | Simulation assertions for D5/D6/D25 pass (I2), **at the adopted K** |\n1048\t| **G5** | Memory budget (I6a) holds on T-scale. **Runs nightly**, so it gates the nightly build, not each commit — see the cadence note below |\n1049\t| **G6** | Throughput budgets (§13.1) hold on T-physical-rig — release only |\n1050\t| **G7** | `python3 docs/research/sim/ge_cost_model.py --check` passes — **the plan's §3.1/§4 numbers match what the model computes**. This exists because every critical defect found in review was a bookkeeping failure attached to correct reasoning; making the numbers executable removes the class |\n1051\t\n1052\t**All-gates-same-commit:** G1–G4 and **G7** MUST pass on the *same* commit — these are\n1053\tfast. G5 is nightly and gates the nightly build; G6 is release-only. A green build\n1054\tassembled from different commits is not a green build.\n1055\t\n1056\t### 14.6 Definition of done\n1057\t\n1058\tA phase is done when: its exit criteria (§17) are met; G1–G5 are green on one commit; every\n1059\tnew failure mode has a test; every new error code has a user-facing string; and the plan\n1060\tis updated if any decision changed.\n1061\t\n1062\t**Stop-ship criteria** — do not release if: any A-scenario fails; I1–I10 are unenforced;\n1063\ta data-loss path exists without a test; or the version footer is absent (a user cannot\n1064\ttell what they are running).\n1065\t\n1066\t---\n1067\t\n1068\t## 15. Throughput expectations\n1069\t\n1070\t*Forecasts from research. The committed numbers are §13.1.*\n1071\t\n1072\t| Stage | Approach | Expected | Regime |\n1073\t|---|---|---|---|\n1074\t| — | Single QR (what most projects do) | 1–9 KB/s | handheld, matches TXQR |\n1075\t| **1** | **Tiled monochrome QR** | **20–45 KB/s** | tripod, laptop→phone |\n1076\t| **2** | **+ RGB channel tripling** | **35–90 KB/s** | tripod |\n1077\t| **3** | **libcimbar-derived codec** | **~106 KB/s** | libcimbar's published figure, monitor→phone. **Its advantage is frame rate, not density** — see below |\n1078\t| — | Phone-to-phone research SOTA | ~40 KB/s | lab, mounted |\n1079\t| — | All-time lab record (PixNet) | 12 Mb/s | **30\" LCD + 24 MP DSLR — not comparable** |\n1080\t\n1081\t**Stage 3's rationale — corrected.** An earlier revision of this section claimed *\"QR is denser\n1082\tper pixel than libcimbar\"* (0.0794 vs 0.0741 bits/screen px²) and used it to push symbology to\n1083\tlast place. **That comparison was invalid, and in exactly the way AP1 warns about:** the 0.0794\n1084\tfigure is QR v16-L at **3** screen px/module, below this plan's own ≥ 4 camera px/module decode\n1085\tfloor.
